references.observation: The dated southwest view shows the same three title characters and wave plinth in the open air. Bronze-toned tubular rails have low balusters, round feet and corner posts. A square dark sign stands behind the rail. Two pale paths curve behind the apron.
The article records that the garden stele was among the stone monuments given protective shelters since 2017.

map.basis: Uses the current draft as a search area only. PMTiles records the canal and main paths. A dated location and heading need a matched path junction or feature.

officialVisitorMap.observation: The guide locates the Silkworm Deity Temple by the canal and shows a curving branch from the canal path toward the Naval Training School. The stele apron has no individual marker. The two curves in the dated photograph lack a securely matched junction on the guide or PMTiles.
officialVisitorMap.scope: Modern visitor context for the historical trial.

limitations: The model depicts the photographed appearance on 29 March 2006. It estimates the rail, sign and pavement dimensions from the picture.

The photograph guides the Chinese title and the line layout of the bilingual panel. The small Chinese and English body copy is unresolved, so only its spacing, contrast and line lengths are represented. Modern close photographs supply the surviving tablet and plinth detail.

The historic camera view shows the open garden paths and a tiled white wall. The immediate path junction has no independent PMTiles feature. The exact historical and current map anchors remain provisional.

panel.title: 耕织图石碑
panel.observedLayout: Five large Chinese title characters, four smaller Chinese rows, then an English heading and seven smaller English rows.
panel.scope: The photograph guides the Chinese title. A perspective-corrected crop traces the visible ink of the smaller Chinese and English text at the photograph’s resolution. The body copy remains unreadable.
